shadows.name: focus-inner-ring
shadows.purpose: The only box-shadow in the system. Zero blur, zero offset; it keeps the 2px CH1 focus outline legible on every ground.

motion.name: state-change

motion.name: nav-bracket
motion.purpose: The header's active-section cursor rules taking color.

motion.name: cursor-sweep
motion.purpose: The measurement cursors sweeping in from ∓50vw to bracket a targeted record row. They stop at rest and stay; a dropped cursor does not fade.

motion.name: skip-link
motion.purpose: The skip link dropping into view on focus. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
The page is one continuous instrument record. Every claim is placed on it as a measured event — value, unit, scope, date, venue, author position, status — so nothing is asserted without its measurement beside it. The reader is not being sold to; they are reading a trace off a panel.

The owned idea is one line: a signal at rest is a straight line at the bottom of the frame, and that line is simultaneously the page's structural baseline and the dragon's ground. The Charizard walks the design instead of standing in front of it. The hero name sits on a rule that steps high at its right end; the bottom lane of the viewport is kept empty on purpose; at wide widths the right margin is declared with a hairline rather than left as slack.

The previous build painted a fixed graticule field behind everything. The owner removed it. body::before and the four --grat data URIs are gone, and with them the grid-minor / grid-major colors, which were never custom properties — they were literal strokes inside those URIs. The 9px module and the ground line stayed. The world lost its wallpaper and kept its geometry, and it reads quieter for it.

One device, repeated, is the handwriting: the measurement strip / readout cell / leader tick family appears in the hero, in two work entries, on four project rows and once in DocsHunt. Density is deliberately uneven — Publications is the dense passage, the merged Toolkit & Recognition band is the reader's breath — because a real record is not uniformly interesting, and two places break the grammar on purpose with no caption.
keyCharacteristics: No background field, no wallpaper, no texture: --field is bare, and the only fixed painted mark on the page is the 2px ground line at bottom: 12px.
One committed channel color (CH1 teal-cyan) carries traces, axis, links, cursors, chips and focus; --sig-2 is a darker/lighter step of the same channel, not a second hue.
Orange is withheld from the entire page. It means only "Charizard is here."
Zero shadows. Depth is tint steps and rule weights.
Status is coded by dash pattern before it is coded by color.
A width axis, not a second font family, is the voice.
Nothing is fixed or sticky at the bottom of the viewport, ever.

rules.name: The Withheld Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange appears nowhere on the page. --accent is declared, contrast-checked, and spent entirely on the dragon's startle mark and his toggle's focus ring. The moment a warm value shows up in site chrome, the pet stops being the highest-contrast event on the screen and the palette loses its point.

rules.name: The One Channel Rule
rules.body: CH1 (--sig) carries every signal-bearing mark. --sig-2 is the same channel one step darker or lighter, and it is hover only. --signal is the pet's. A second hue is not available — if something needs to stand out it gets a rule weight or a tint step, never a new angle on the wheel.

rules.name: The Faint-Is-Metadata Rule
rules.body: --ink-faint is reserved for the axis ticks. A date, venue, author, or status is content and lives at --ink-soft or --ink. Demoting a fact to faint is how a record stops being readable.

rules.name: The Two-Hairline Rule
rules.body: --line is decoration (section rules, the header rule, the lane rule) and belongs to pet.css as well; --line-2 is structure (row dividers, cell gaps inside a bordered container). Do not swap them, and never delete --line to "simplify" — the toggle reads it.

rules.name: The Twelve-Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing functional renders below 12px. 0.75rem is the floor and it is exactly 12px at the default root. Undersized UI text is designed out, not patched later.

rules.name: The Aligning-Digits Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is for digits and identifiers that must align in a column or read as instrument annotation: year ticks, measured values, venues, statuses, date ranges, repo slugs, and the one note. It is never prose, never decorative small-caps chrome. The previous build's two prose exceptions died with the elements that carried them; the allowance is now closed, not extended.

rules.name: The Width-Not-Weight Rule
rules.body: Emphasis in headings comes from the width axis (112 / 118 / 125) at a constant 640 weight. Reaching for a heavier weight or a second family to make something louder is off-system.

rules.name: The Plain-Heading Rule. Section headings are plain nouns (Work, Publications, Projects, Toolkit, Recognition) by the owner's decision of 2026-09-08; counts and spans live in the hero cells and the rail ticks, never in a heading, and never as a slogan.
rules.body: The Plain-Heading Rule. Section headings are plain nouns (Work, Publications, Projects, Toolkit, Recognition) by the owner's decision of 2026-09-08; counts and spans live in the hero cells and the rail ticks, never in a heading, and never as a slogan.

rules.name: The Nine-Pixel Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Section padding, band gaps, row gaps, the lane, and the footer tail are multiples of 9. Component interiors are free. A new section that isn't on the module is a mistake; a new cell that isn't, is not.

rules.name: The Nothing-At-The-Bottom Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this site is position: fixed or sticky at the bottom of the viewport. Top-pinned is legal; bottom-pinned is a contract violation. The bottom ~96px belongs to the dragon and to the 🔥 toggle in the bottom-left corner.

rules.name: The Declared-Margin Rule
rules.body: At ≥1200px the right 120px of the record column is empty by declaration, with a hairline naming the edge. Nothing prose, interactive, or plate-edged goes past it.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Zero blur radius anywhere. A surface that needs to separate from its ground gets a tint step or a rule weight. The hairline-border-plus-wide-soft-shadow card is the exact tell this world was built to avoid, and one box-shadow: 0 4px 24px undoes it.

rules.name: The Earned-Cell Rule
rules.body: A readout cell, a strip, or a chip appears because a real number or a real record exists behind it. Adding one to balance a row visually turns an instrument into a decoration.

rules.name: The Deliberate-Seam Rule
rules.body: Two places break the grammar on purpose and ship with no caption, no note, and no apology: the JKAIA row, which has no artifact furniture and states in one plain sentence that the paper was non-archival and there is no link; and the DocsHunt entry, which has one readout cell and no findings list at all. They are not omissions and they are not bugs. A future edit that "completes" either one deletes the evidence that a person wrote this record.

rules.name: The Three-Cell Ceiling Rule
rules.body: A strip never exceeds three cells. Study-scale numbers belong on the record row that carries the author position, not in a fourth cell.

dos: Do put a new band's vertical rhythm on the 9px module (45 / 54 / 27 / 18) and leave cell interiors alone.
Do give every container a 1px --line-strong edge and a --surface ground, and separate its cells with gap: 1px over a --line-2 background.
Do code state with a line pattern first (solid / dashed / dotted) and color second, so the record survives desaturation — and write the status in words beside it.
Do reuse the measurement strip / readout cell / leader tick family for anything new that is measured. Repetition is the point; a new device is not.
Do keep every interactive element on the 7px key radius and everything readable square.
Do put mono only where digits, dates, venues, statuses or repo slugs align, and keep the type floor at 0.75rem.
Do give a section heading a count and a span, and let the notation explain itself.

Do keep the hero name as real uppercase text in .hero h1 — one text node, no child elements, no pseudo-element, .step a sibling — with the "Archivo Fallback" stack and the px clamp intact, in the first viewport, with clear space to its right.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow with any blur or offset. The only shadow in this file is the focus inner ring.
Don't introduce orange, amber, or any warm hue into page chrome. --accent belongs to the dragon.
Don't make --sig-2 a second hue again. It is a lightness step of CH1, and dark --sig is pinned to cyan (hue ~188–200°) because pet.css hardcodes rgba(96,205,255) for the tail glow.
Don't re-introduce a background field, wallpaper, texture, or graticule layer. The owner removed it; --field is bare.
Don't use z-index ≥ 999 — or, honestly, above 20. Current ceiling: skip link 20, header 10, ground line −1.
Don't fix or stick anything to the bottom of the viewport, and don't let content encroach on the bottom lane or on the declared 120px right margin at ≥1200px.

Don't add an uppercase kicker or eyebrow above a heading, a legend line that explains the page's own notation, a tag-pill row, or a labelled NAME/ROLE/LOCATION grid. All four were removed; do not bring the devices back under new names.
Don't number the sections (01, 02). Sequence is carried by real year ticks in the axis gutter.
Don't convert Projects or Publications into a card grid, and don't equalize section density — unevenness is load-bearing.
Don't add fade-up, parallax, or scroll-triggered reveals. Motion in this world is one cursor sweep that stops, and a 0.16s color change.
Don't demote a date, venue, author, or status to --ink-faint, and don't spend --signal or --accent on the page.
Don't add a third font family or reach for a heavier weight — emphasis comes from the width axis.
Don't hide the author position, the status, or the N / M string at any width, and don't turn any of them into a title attribute.
Don't add any <input>, <textarea>, contenteditable, or free-text <select>, ever, and don't take :target away from .record li.
